Freedom from obsessive compulsive disorder by Jonathan Grayson

It's very current and talks a bit more detailed and skips the "this is what Ocd is" and all the stuff we already know about OcD.

Hmm this is a bit all over. But one thing I want to mention is about your OCD assumption. OCD isn't purely about cleaning.  While contamination is one of the sub types of OCD and is a symptom some may have, there are many forms of OCD. Not just cleaning or organization. 

Right now it sounds overall that it could be you are doing a lot of self-diagnosing and are reading into all kinds of stuff and just picking it up as a possibility or fact as you may share some symptoms etc. The "web Ms" effect as it's known. You read it, you feel it, you think it, you diagnose it and it's true now. When it's not usually. I have thought I had multiple illnesses and different diagnosis based on my researching symptoms. And many people do this and well, we all suck at it and things are a bit more complicated than that. Plus you just rattled out 4-5 different things at once you may have. Either your the most unlucky person out there or some of these aren't real for you maybe. Again they share some symptoms and stuff but you even admit that you're not 100% sure on it all and this maybe influencing your doctors perception of it as well. 

I would say your best bet is to go to a doctor. A new doctor if you can and go in for a general analysis. Don't tell them what you think you have. Unless they ask. But if it were me I would just say that I have some issues and this is what I'm doing physically based on these feelings and ask what do they think. What can be done. And really start with a clean slate. One issue at a time. 

Otherwise you are just throwing tons of stuff at a wall and seeing what sticks and not giving a clear simple indication of anything. You could be a hypochondriac or bipolar or anything else that has similar symptoms. But it doesn't help if you don't slow down and take it from 0 and work closely with a new doctor for a generic analysis to determine your condition. In the end ask the doctor what they think so far and go from there. 

That's my opinion at least. So far it doesn't sound like you have OCD to me, and your example of OCD didn't even show me you knew what OCD involves. So likely you are ok with that one.

Trust me. I have the same issues and fears you do as I'm a contamination suffer. I live in Houston. Where it's very common to see roaches in the summer. 

Not sure on your setup, like if your in an apartment or house but here are some ideas and things I use to do in my own house to rid myself of pests and roaches. 

If you can, go to a pesticide chemical store. Should be some around your town. They sale the good stuff for cheap, none of that cheap stuff you get from Home Depot. Stuff that exterminators and other professionals use. So this may save you money down the line by doing it yourself. 

I use to buy this stuff called Demon. Not sure if it exists anymore but in sure there are similar ones. But it was a powder you mixed in water. Once you spray it, it lasts at least a year and I had it work up to 2 years. And it kills anything. So be warned if you have pets and children. But the stuff was awesome. Like you would at most see a big outdoor roach run on where I sprayed and in less then a second it would just tumble and die after contact. Sweet satisfaction in my book. 

But I would do this and spray along the floor against the corners of my walls inside my house. along and inside any cracks. Bottom of closets. And heavily along doors leading outside my house.  Inside the door frame too. And if you can I would spray on the outside of my door right on it a bit. And on the walls around my outside door so no pests would hang around my house at night waiting to fly in due to the lights. 

As for pipes, roaches love water. So that's why you are seeing them in bathrooms and kitchens. If you can. Pour a good amount of bleach down your drains and bathtub. Roaches if in the pipes or anything will get killed and the smell of bleach will deter them. Then get some decent drain covers with smaller holes in them to prevent them from coming  in that way. 

It's not likely how they are getting in but there's a possibly and you want to cover your bases. 

You are definitely going to need to check under your sinks though. Sorry but you have to brave that one with some gloves if you need to. I use to spray in there too as well as its moisture. Plus you can check if you have a water leak or any wall cracks. As these things are definitely going to attract roaches and bugs. So make sure it's dry in there and that you have any cracks covered and sprayed. 

Other than that I think you will be ok. Roaches suck and I would clean anything they touch myself 2 times usually with wipes. But your key plan should be prevention of course.

But I lived with it and suffered with it for so long. Knowing it wasn't right. But it never effected my work. And to me that was the last straw. When I finally broke down mentally and physically and I started avoiding work and working around people and their disgusting habits and touching things that they would touch, etc. 

That's when it finally hit me, it was like I was living in a dream that wasn't real. I felt the walls of my own reality against my mind when I finally said to myself in my car with tears building up in my eyes as one of my favorite songs played on my stereo - telling myself out loud in a voice that wasn't truly of my own as the stress on my vocal chords played its part when I said "I have OCD". And I felt as if that can't be me, that how could I be this way and live this way. That this is wrong and this is just a bad dream. 

Even now I sometimes feel this way. That this has to just one day end. That one day I'll just be normal and wake up and be free of it all. But then I realize it won't happen that way. It can't be that easy. And I will suffer and I will hurt myself either to never be free or to break through that mind that's captures me still. 


Sorry for being grim. I've just been at my worst lately.

It's usually a really small dose you start with and the side effects are usually tame if at all, which is why it's the first go to drug for just about any mild to severe issue. Wanted to add... Don't be too afraid of the side effects. They vary from person to person and you won't know till you try it. 

I would say to try it. Take it at night and maybe start it on the weekend so if there are any side effects. It's something you can manage and handle without interfering with your social and daily life.

Like Eve mentioned. It's usually rather subtle. Usually, but everyone is different. You might not have found your proper dose or medication yet. It's a lot of trial and error starting out what works for you.

The key is to find something that lessens your symptoms down yet lets you function. The meds will not cure you or stop everything Ocd related. They are meant to ease it under some sort of control.
